target_customer: Commercial laundry operators at the start, and by 2026 commercial warehouse operators needing repetitive packing work
problem: Frontline physical labor is repetitive and hard to staff. Parametric builds bimanual mobile robots that learn tasks from customer feedback.
business_model: Robots and fleet software for commercial operations (pricing not found)

founders.name: Cody Swain
previous_startups: Early non-custodial stablecoin wallet company (raised over 7M per YC profile)

competitors.name: Dyna Robotics
competitors.what: Robot foundation models for commercial manipulation tasks such as napkin and laundry folding on dual-arm hardware
competitors.traction_then: DYNA-1 model debuted April 2025; laundromat deployment in Sacramento

technical_complexity.rationale: Learning manipulation from feedback on bimanual mobile hardware is research-grade and needs hardware, ML and fleet operations.

defensibility.rationale: Operational data from robots working in customer sites could compound, but well-funded foundation model rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dyna Robotics released DYNA 2.1 for commercial laundry shifts in September 2026, a direct overlap; no acquisition of Parametric documented.

market_need_then: Laundromats and warehouses have repetitive labor, and robotics investors funded manipulation startups in 2025, but no Parametric customer revenue was found; the company's site reports autonomy rising from 0 percent in February 2026 to 75 percent of robot time in July 2026.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold vision: physical businesses that run themselves; robot product named Bit and fleet app Bastion

branding.brand_signature: Robot named Bit and fleet app Bastion

brand_strength.rationale: A generic engineering term shared with other companies, offset by named products, with no press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: Autonomous wash-and-fold laundromat in San Francisco
pivots.to: Bimanual mobile robot Bit for commercial warehouse work
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page and an aggregator describe laundry while the company site now describes warehouse tasks.

outcome_analysis: Parametric is an active Fall 2025 company with seven people and no confirmed public funding. It moved from a laundry-first plan to warehouse tasks and reports rapid autonomy gains, but faces funded rivals such as Dyna Robotics, so outcomes depend on hardware reliability and customer deployments.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, Standout) list 500K with Y Combinator as sole investor, labeled pre-seed in one and seed in another; unverified single-source aggregators, so no round is recorded. Some aggregators list Cody Swain as an investor and the 7M figure belongs to his earlier company. The pivot date is approximate and inferred from the difference between YC and aggregator descriptions and the company site.
